RemEx is your remote PC management command center. Control your computer, launch apps, monitor performance, and even view your desktop — all from your phone.\n\nLet\'s get you connected in a few quick steps.

Before you can connect, you need the RemEx host software running on your PC.

Option 1 — RemEx Desktop Client
Download and run Remex.Client.Desktop on your PC. It bundles the host automatically — just launch it and the host starts in the background.

Option 2 — RemEx Host (standalone)
Install and run Remex.Host as a standalone service. This is ideal for headless servers or if you only need the host.

Both are self-contained — no extra runtimes needed. Download the latest publish folder from the GitHub releases page, extract, and run.

The easiest way to connect is automatic discovery.

1. Make sure Remex.Client.Desktop or Remex.Host is running on your PC
2. Ensure both your phone and PC are on the same Wi-Fi network
3. Tap 'Discover Automatically' on the Connection screen

RemEx uses mDNS to detect running hosts on your local network. Your PC's IP and port will be filled in automatically.

If auto-discovery doesn't work, you can connect manually. First, find your PC's local IP address:

Windows:
 Open Command Prompt → type ipconfig
 Look for 'IPv4 Address' (e.g. 192.168.1.42)

macOS:
 System Settings → Network, or run:
 ipconfig getifaddr en0

Linux:
 Run ip addr or hostname -I

You can also see the IP address in the Remex.Client.Desktop window under the connection status section.

Once you have your IP address:

1. Go to the Connection screen (Settings → Connection)
2. Enter your PC's IP address
3. Enter the port (default is 5005)
4. Tap 'Save & Connect'

RemEx will establish a connection and you'll see your PC's status appear on the dashboard.

Remember: Remex.Client.Desktop or Remex.Host must be running on the target PC for the connection to succeed.

You're ready to take control.

From the dashboard you can monitor system stats, launch apps, manage tasks, and stream your desktop remotely.

Head to Personalization to customize your theme, card shapes, fonts, and colors.

Check out the FAQ in Settings if you run into any issues. Enjoy RemEx!

What do I need to run on my PC?

You need either Remex.Client.Desktop or Remex.Host running on your PC.

• Remex.Client.Desktop — The full desktop app that bundles the host automatically. Just launch it and the host starts in the background on port 5005.

• Remex.Host — A standalone headless service, ideal for servers or background-only use.

Both are self-contained (all runtimes included) — just extract the publish folder and run. Download from the GitHub releases page.
How do I find my PC\'s IP address?

Windows:
Open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig'. Look for the 'IPv4 Address' line under your active network adapter (e.g. 192.168.1.42).

macOS:
Go to System Settings → Network and look at the connected interface, or open Terminal and run: ipconfig getifaddr en0

Linux:
Open a terminal and run: ip addr or hostname -I

You can also see the IP directly in the Remex.Client.Desktop window.
Auto-discovery isn\'t finding my PC. What should I check?

1. Make sure Remex.Client.Desktop or Remex.Host is actually running on your PC.
2. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi / LAN network.
3. On Android 13+, the NEARBY_WIFI_DEVICES permission must be granted. RemEx will prompt for this when you tap 'Discover Automatically'.
4. Some routers have 'AP Isolation' or 'Client Isolation' enabled, which blocks device-to-device communication. Check your router settings.
5. Corporate or guest Wi-Fi networks often block mDNS traffic. Try using a personal or home network instead.

The default port is 5005. If Remex.Client.Desktop finds port 5005 in use, it will fall back to 5006. You can see the active port in the desktop client\'s window.\n\nIf you changed the port on the host side, make sure to enter the matching port in the Connection screen on this app.
What is the Access Key for?

The Access Key is an optional authentication token. If you set an access key on the host (in Remex.Host settings), you must enter the same key here to connect.\n\nIf you haven\'t configured one on the host, leave this field empty.
Can I connect over the internet (not just LAN)?

RemEx is designed for local network (LAN) use. To connect over the internet you would need to set up port forwarding on your router for port 5005 (or whichever port you use) and use your public IP address.\n\nImportant: Exposing the port to the internet is a security risk. If you do this, always enable the Access Key for authentication. A VPN is the recommended approach for remote access.
Remote Desktop is laggy or not working. What can I do?

• Lower the Quality slider in Connection → Remote Desktop Defaults.
• Reduce the Target FPS (15–20 FPS is sufficient for most use cases).
• Lower the Scale to reduce the resolution being streamed.
• Make sure your PC supports the screen capture backend: DXGI on Windows, X11/Wayland on Linux.
• Check that you're on a fast, local Wi-Fi network (5 GHz preferred).

Wake-on-LAN lets you power on your PC remotely by sending a "magic packet" over the network.

To use it:
1. Enable WOL in your PC's BIOS/UEFI settings.
2. Enable WOL in your network adapter's properties (Windows: Device Manager → Network Adapter → Power Management).
3. Enter your PC's MAC address in the Connection screen.
4. Use the 'Wake PC' card on the dashboard or the Remote Control screen.
How do I customize the app\'s appearance?

Go to the Personalization screen (tap the gear FAB on the dashboard or navigate via the overflow menu → Settings).

You can change:
• Theme palette and color seed
• Card corner radius and shape presets
• Font family and scale
• Card opacity
• Dark/light/system theme mode
